claim: The lymphocytic infiltrate in melanoma is classified morphologically into 'brisk', 'non-brisk' and 'absent' patterns.
source: In melanoma, the lymphocytic infiltrate is a prognostic parameter classified morphologically into 'brisk', 'non-brisk' and 'absent' entailing a functional association that has never been proved.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract and introduction, referencing established classification systems.

claim: The functional association of the brisk/non-brisk/absent morphological classification has never been proved.
source: In melanoma, the lymphocytic infiltrate is a prognostic parameter classified morphologically into 'brisk', 'non-brisk' and 'absent' entailing a functional association that has never been proved.
evidence: The authors explicitly state this gap in knowledge in the abstract.

claim: Anti-PD-1 immunotherapy supports activated T cells.
source: Recently, it has been shown that lymphocytic populations can be very heterogeneous, and that anti-PD-1 immunotherapy supports activated T cells.
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to Krieg et al., 2018 in the introduction.

claim: The brisk and non-brisk patterns are heterogeneous functional categories that can be further sub-classified into active, transitional or exhausted.
source: We observed that the brisk and non-brisk patterns are heterogeneous functional categories that can be further sub-classified into active, transitional or exhausted.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by data in Figure 2.

claim: The classification of primary melanomas based on the functional paradigm shows correlation with spontaneous regression.
source: The classification of primary melanomas based on the functional paradigm also shows correlation with spontaneous regression, and an improved prognostic value when compared to that of the brisk classification.
evidence: This finding is stated in the abstract and supported by data in Figure 3 and Table 1.

claim: The functional classification has improved prognostic value when compared to the brisk morphological classification.
source: The classification of primary melanomas based on the functional paradigm also shows correlation with spontaneous regression, and an improved prognostic value when compared to that of the brisk classification.
evidence: This is demonstrated by survival analysis showing log-rank p-value of 0.079 for functional classification vs 0.36 for brisk classification (Figure 2E).

claim: The 'brisk' pattern has a better prognosis compared to the 'non-brisk' or 'absent' pattern.
source: The 'brisk' pattern (diffuse or complete peripheral TILs infiltration) has a better prognosis compared to the 'non-brisk' (tumour areas with TILs alternate with areas without TILs) or to the 'absent' pattern (no TILs or no contact with melanoma cells) (Clark et al., 1989; Clemente et al., 1996; Mihm et al., 1996).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to Clark et al., 1989; Clemente et al., 1996; Mihm et al., 1996.

claim: Morphology alone cannot determine the activation status of tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes.
source: There are multiple pitfalls in the purely morphological evaluation of TILs (Bosisio and van den Oord, 2017), but the most important one is that morphology alone cannot determine their activation status.
evidence: This is stated as a key limitation in the introduction with citation to Bosisio and van den Oord, 2017.

claim: The contact between cytotoxic lymphocytes and melanoma does not always lead to tumor eradication but can result in T cell inactivation due to immune modulation.
source: The contact between cytotoxic lymphocytes (Tcy) and melanoma does not always lead to tumor eradication but, due to immune modulation, can also result in Tcy inactivation.
evidence: This is stated as a conceptual framework in the introduction.

claim: Exhausted cytotoxic T cells would be morphologically present and indistinguishable from active lymphocytes.
source: These 'exhausted' Tcy would still be morphologically present, indistinguishable from active lymphocytes.
evidence: This is stated as a key problem with morphological assessment in the introduction.

claim: The functional status of circulating inflammatory cells can completely change when entering the tumor site.
source: Though, the functional status of circulating inflammatory cells can completely change entering the tumour site (Buggert et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated with citation to Buggert et al., 2018.

claim: The study characterized the immune landscape in primary melanoma using a panel of 39 immune markers applied on one single tissue section through the MILAN technique.
source: Here, we characterize the immune landscape at single cell-level in primary melanoma based on a panel of 39 immune markers applied on one single tissue section through a high-dimensional multiplexing method (Cattoretti et al., 2001; Bolognesi et al., 2017), a RT-PCR expression evaluation and a shotgun proteomic analysis.
evidence: This describes the methodology used in the study with citations to Cattoretti et al., 2001; Bolognesi et al., 2017.

claim: Each CD8+ cell was classified as part of a spectrum ranging from 'active' (CD69high and/or OX40high) to 'exhausted' (TIM3highCD69lowOX40low).
source: We classified each CD8+ cell in the TMA cores as part of a spectrum ('functional status') ranging from 'active' (CD69high and/or OX40high) to 'exhausted' (TIM3highCD69lowOX40low) (Figure 2A–D and Supplementary Data 1).
evidence: This describes the functional classification method with reference to Figure 2.

claim: 17 out of 60 cores were defined as active, 23 out of 60 in transition, and 20 out of 60 defined as exhausted.
source: The assignation of a functional status to each core in the TMA ('core status', see Materials and methods) yielded 17/60 cores defined as active, 23/60 in transition, and 20/60 defined as exhausted.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the functional analysis.

claim: From 21 patients with multiple cores, 10 showed homogeneous core statuses and 11 showed heterogeneity.
source: From the 21 remaining patients, 10/21 showed homogeneous core statuses: four active, five in transition, and one exhausted; and 11/21 showed heterogeneity.
evidence: This describes intra-patient heterogeneity observed in the study.

claim: Patient classification based on functional status has an improved prognostic performance (log-rank p.value = 0.079) when compared with the brisk morphological classification (log-rank p.value = 0.36).
source: Correlation with clinical survival (overall survival, OS) showed that patient classification based on functional status has an improved prognostic performance (log-rank p.value = 0.079) when compared with the brisk morphological classification (log-rank p.value = 0.36) (Figure 2E).
evidence: This is a key finding supported by survival analysis data shown in Figure 2E.

claim: Patients in the 'Active' group had better prognosis than patients in the 'Exhausted' group in the SKCM TCGA dataset (log-rank p-value=0.0082).
source: Also repeating the survival analysis in the SKCM TCGA data set confirmed that the patients in the 'Active' group had better prognosis than the patients in the 'Exhausted' group (log-rank p-value=0.0082) validating the results obtained with our dataset (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a validation result using an independent dataset shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: Late regression areas showed significant differences in the mean level of activation compared to early regression (p=0.022) and no regression (p=0.031).
source: Late regression areas indeed showed significant differences in the mean level of activation of the cores as compared to early regression (p=0.022) and no regression (p=0.031).
evidence: This is a statistical finding from the analysis of regression areas shown in Figure 3 and Table 1.

claim: No significant differences were found between early regression and no regression in terms of activation levels.
source: No significant differences were instead found between early regression and no regression (Figure 3A,B).
evidence: This is stated as a negative result in the analysis of regression areas.

claim: Higher levels of activation were found in Lentigo Maligna Melanoma (p=0.02).
source: Higher levels of activation were found in Lentigo Maligna Melanoma (p=0.02).
evidence: This is a statistical finding from the histopathological parameter analysis.

claim: Only three LMM cores from two patients were included in the dataset, so no definite conclusions can be drawn about LMM.
source: However, since only three LMM cores from two patients were included in our data set, no definite conclusions can be drawn from this data.
evidence: The authors explicitly acknowledge this limitation.

claim: Brisk cases were significantly enriched in B cells (p-val = 0.041).
source: Brisk cases were significantly enriched in BC (p-val = 0.041), TIM3+cDC1 (p-val = 0.024), macrophages (p-val = 0.043) (including the proliferating subgroup (p-val = 0.034)), NK (p-val = 0.011), anergic Tcy (p-val = 0.039) and proliferating Tcy (p-val = 0.006) (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is a statistical finding from phenotypic analysis shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Brisk cases were significantly enriched in TIM3+cDC1 (p-val = 0.024).
source: Brisk cases were significantly enriched in BC (p-val = 0.041), TIM3+cDC1 (p-val = 0.024), macrophages (p-val = 0.043) (including the proliferating subgroup (p-val = 0.034)), NK (p-val = 0.011), anergic Tcy (p-val = 0.039) and proliferating Tcy (p-val = 0.006) (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is a statistical finding from phenotypic analysis shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Brisk cases were significantly enriched in macrophages (p-val = 0.043).
source: Brisk cases were significantly enriched in BC (p-val = 0.041), TIM3+cDC1 (p-val = 0.024), macrophages (p-val = 0.043) (including the proliferating subgroup (p-val = 0.034)), NK (p-val = 0.011), anergic Tcy (p-val = 0.039) and proliferating Tcy (p-val = 0.006) (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is a statistical finding from phenotypic analysis shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Brisk cases were significantly enriched in NK cells (p-val = 0.011).
source: Brisk cases were significantly enriched in BC (p-val = 0.041), TIM3+cDC1 (p-val = 0.024), macrophages (p-val = 0.043) (including the proliferating subgroup (p-val = 0.034)), NK (p-val = 0.011), anergic Tcy (p-val = 0.039) and proliferating Tcy (p-val = 0.006) (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is a statistical finding from phenotypic analysis shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Brisk cases were significantly enriched in anergic Tcy (p-val = 0.039).
source: Brisk cases were significantly enriched in BC (p-val = 0.041), TIM3+cDC1 (p-val = 0.024), macrophages (p-val = 0.043) (including the proliferating subgroup (p-val = 0.034)), NK (p-val = 0.011), anergic Tcy (p-val = 0.039) and proliferating Tcy (p-val = 0.006) (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is a statistical finding from phenotypic analysis shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Brisk cases were significantly enriched in proliferating Tcy (p-val = 0.006).
source: Brisk cases were significantly enriched in BC (p-val = 0.041), TIM3+cDC1 (p-val = 0.024), macrophages (p-val = 0.043) (including the proliferating subgroup (p-val = 0.034)), NK (p-val = 0.011), anergic Tcy (p-val = 0.039) and proliferating Tcy (p-val = 0.006) (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is a statistical finding from phenotypic analysis shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Active cores had higher percentages of active Tcy (p-val <0.001).
source: Active cores had, together with more active Tcy (p-val <0.001), higher percentages of Tcy in transition (p-val = 0.030), transition cores more Th (p-val = 0.057), while exhausted cases had more TIM3+Tregs (p-val = 0.018) and more proliferating melanoma cells (p-val = 0.045) (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is a statistical finding from phenotypic analysis shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Active cores had higher percentages of Tcy in transition (p-val = 0.030).
source: Active cores had, together with more active Tcy (p-val <0.001), higher percentages of Tcy in transition (p-val = 0.030), transition cores more Th (p-val = 0.057), while exhausted cases had more TIM3+Tregs (p-val = 0.018) and more proliferating melanoma cells (p-val = 0.045) (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is a statistical finding from phenotypic analysis shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Exhausted cases had more TIM3+Tregs (p-val = 0.018).
source: Active cores had, together with more active Tcy (p-val <0.001), higher percentages of Tcy in transition (p-val = 0.030), transition cores more Th (p-val = 0.057), while exhausted cases had more TIM3+Tregs (p-val = 0.018) and more proliferating melanoma cells (p-val = 0.045) (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is a statistical finding from phenotypic analysis shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Exhausted cases had more proliferating melanoma cells (p-val = 0.045).
source: Active cores had, together with more active Tcy (p-val <0.001), higher percentages of Tcy in transition (p-val = 0.030), transition cores more Th (p-val = 0.057), while exhausted cases had more TIM3+Tregs (p-val = 0.018) and more proliferating melanoma cells (p-val = 0.045) (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is a statistical finding from phenotypic analysis shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Macrophages and epithelial cells were most often located in strict proximity to melanoma cells without differences among functional or morphologic categories.
source: Macrophages and epithelial cells were in general most often located in strict proximity to the melanoma cells, without differences among the functional or morphologic categories.
evidence: This is a finding from neighborhood analysis.

claim: Brisk cases showed more Tcy in close proximity to melanoma cells than non-brisk cases.
source: Brisk cases showed more Tcy in close proximity to melanoma cells than non-brisk cases, as expected (Figure 5E).
evidence: This is a finding from neighborhood analysis shown in Figure 5E.

claim: Brisk cases had a higher prevalence of transition and active Tcy in contact with melanoma cells compared with non-brisk cases (Active/Exhausted ratio: Brisk = 2.108762, Non-Brisk = 1.331195).
source: Interestingly, brisk cases had a higher prevalence specifically of transition and active Tcy in contact with melanoma cells compared with non-brisk cases (Active/Exhausted ratio: Brisk = 2.108762, Non-Brisk = 1.331195), that instead had relatively more exhausted and anergic cells in contact with melanoma cells (Active/Anergic ratio: Brisk = 1.743081, NonBrisk = 0.7704947).
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from neighborhood analysis.

claim: Non-brisk cases had relatively more exhausted and anergic cells in contact with melanoma cells (Active/Anergic ratio: Brisk = 1.743081, NonBrisk = 0.7704947).
source: Interestingly, brisk cases had a higher prevalence specifically of transition and active Tcy in contact with melanoma cells compared with non-brisk cases (Active/Exhausted ratio: Brisk = 2.108762, Non-Brisk = 1.331195), that instead had relatively more exhausted and anergic cells in contact with melanoma cells (Active/Anergic ratio: Brisk = 1.743081, NonBrisk = 0.7704947).
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from neighborhood analysis.

claim: The most abundant cell population consisted of melanoma cells (41.76%).
source: The most abundant cell population consisted of melanoma cells (41.76%).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from phenotypic identification shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Macrophages represented 11.48% of the cell population.
source: The second most abundant cell type were the macrophages ('Macroph', CD68+CD163+Lysozyme+HLA-DR+, 11.48%), one quarter of them expressing the immunosuppressive marker TIM3.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from phenotypic identification shown in Figure 4A.

claim: One quarter of macrophages expressed the immunosuppressive marker TIM3.
source: The second most abundant cell type were the macrophages ('Macroph', CD68+CD163+Lysozyme+HLA-DR+, 11.48%), one quarter of them expressing the immunosuppressive marker TIM3.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from phenotypic identification.

claim: Epithelial cells represented 8.4% of the population.
source: Epithelial cells represented 8.4% of the population of our data set.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from phenotypic identification shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Cytotoxic T cells (Tcy) accounted for 11.19% of all cells.
source: Tcy (CD3+CD8+) and T helpers ('Th', CD3+CD4+FOXP3-) were the most abundant subtypes, accounting respectively for 11.19% and 10.10% of all the cells, while regulatory T cells ('Treg', CD3+CD4+FOXP3+) represented 2.82% of the cells.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from phenotypic identification shown in Figure 4A.

claim: T helper cells (Th) accounted for 10.10% of all cells.
source: Tcy (CD3+CD8+) and T helpers ('Th', CD3+CD4+FOXP3-) were the most abundant subtypes, accounting respectively for 11.19% and 10.10% of all the cells, while regulatory T cells ('Treg', CD3+CD4+FOXP3+) represented 2.82% of the cells.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from phenotypic identification shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Regulatory T cells (Treg) represented 2.82% of the cells.
source: Tcy (CD3+CD8+) and T helpers ('Th', CD3+CD4+FOXP3-) were the most abundant subtypes, accounting respectively for 11.19% and 10.10% of all the cells, while regulatory T cells ('Treg', CD3+CD4+FOXP3+) represented 2.82% of the cells.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from phenotypic identification shown in Figure 4A.

claim: T follicular helpers (Tfh) represented 2.57% of the cells.
source: We interpreted the last T cell cluster as T follicular helpers ('Tfh', CXCL13+PD1+, 2.57%) even though this cluster did not express the full Tfh phenotype.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from phenotypic identification shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Within Tcy, 16.1% of all lymphocytes were active (CD69+OX40+/-).
source: Within Tcy, we could identify the active (CD69+OX40+/-, 16,1% of all the lymphocytes), transition (balanced expression of both exhaustion and expression markers, 29.6%) and exhausted (high expression of LAG3 and/or TIM3, low/absent CD69 and OX40, 12.8%) functional subgroups.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from functional subgroup analysis.

claim: Within Tcy, 29.6% of all lymphocytes were in transition.
source: Within Tcy, we could identify the active (CD69+OX40+/-, 16,1% of all the lymphocytes), transition (balanced expression of both exhaustion and expression markers, 29.6%) and exhausted (high expression of LAG3 and/or TIM3, low/absent CD69 and OX40, 12.8%) functional subgroups.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from functional subgroup analysis.

claim: Within Tcy, 12.8% of all lymphocytes were exhausted (high expression of LAG3 and/or TIM3, low/absent CD69 and OX40).
source: Within Tcy, we could identify the active (CD69+OX40+/-, 16,1% of all the lymphocytes), transition (balanced expression of both exhaustion and expression markers, 29.6%) and exhausted (high expression of LAG3 and/or TIM3, low/absent CD69 and OX40, 12.8%) functional subgroups.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from functional subgroup analysis.

claim: A clonally expanding Tcy subgroup represented 6% of lymphocytes.
source: Moreover, we found a clonally expanding subgroup (6%), and one with low or absent expression of all functional markers, that we defined as 'anergic' (34,9%) but that could represent also naive T cells.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from functional subgroup analysis.

claim: An 'anergic' Tcy subgroup with low or absent expression of all functional markers represented 34.9% of lymphocytes.
source: Moreover, we found a clonally expanding subgroup (6%), and one with low or absent expression of all functional markers, that we defined as 'anergic' (34,9%) but that could represent also naive T cells.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from functional subgroup analysis.

claim: The 'anergic' Tcy subgroup could represent naive T cells.
source: Moreover, we found a clonally expanding subgroup (6%), and one with low or absent expression of all functional markers, that we defined as 'anergic' (34,9%) but that could represent also naive T cells.
evidence: The authors acknowledge this alternative interpretation.

claim: NK cells were extremely infrequent (0.51%) in melanoma.
source: NK cells, as expected in melanoma, were extremely infrequent (0.51%), and even more infrequent were the B cells ('BC', CD20+), that represented 0.12% of the total.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from phenotypic identification shown in Figure 4A.

claim: B cells represented 0.12% of the total cell population.
source: NK cells, as expected in melanoma, were extremely infrequent (0.51%), and even more infrequent were the B cells ('BC', CD20+), that represented 0.12% of the total.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from phenotypic identification shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Plasma cells represented 1.19% of the total cell population.
source: The CD20 negative cells characterized by high expression of IRF4 and Blimp1 ('PC', 1,19%) were interpreted as plasma cells (Caicedo et al., 2017).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from phenotypic identification shown in Figure 4A with citation to Caicedo et al., 2017.

claim: Classical dendritic cells type 1 (cDC1) represented 4.13% of cells.
source: Finally, we could identify among the dendritic cell group the classical dendritic cells type 1 ('cDC1', CD141+CD4+IRF8+, 4.13%), classical dendritic cells type 2 ('cDC2', CD1c+CD4+HLA-DR+, 2.41%), Langerhans cells ('Lang', CD1a+Langerin+, 2.13%), and plasmacytoid dendritic cells ('pDC', CD123+, 0.33%).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from phenotypic identification shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Classical dendritic cells type 2 (cDC2) represented 2.41% of cells.
source: Finally, we could identify among the dendritic cell group the classical dendritic cells type 1 ('cDC1', CD141+CD4+IRF8+, 4.13%), classical dendritic cells type 2 ('cDC2', CD1c+CD4+HLA-DR+, 2.41%), Langerhans cells ('Lang', CD1a+Langerin+, 2.13%), and plasmacytoid dendritic cells ('pDC', CD123+, 0.33%).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from phenotypic identification shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Langerhans cells represented 2.13% of cells.
source: Finally, we could identify among the dendritic cell group the classical dendritic cells type 1 ('cDC1', CD141+CD4+IRF8+, 4.13%), classical dendritic cells type 2 ('cDC2', CD1c+CD4+HLA-DR+, 2.41%), Langerhans cells ('Lang', CD1a+Langerin+, 2.13%), and plasmacytoid dendritic cells ('pDC', CD123+, 0.33%).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from phenotypic identification shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Plasmacytoid dendritic cells (pDC) represented 0.33% of cells.
source: Finally, we could identify among the dendritic cell group the classical dendritic cells type 1 ('cDC1', CD141+CD4+IRF8+, 4.13%), classical dendritic cells type 2 ('cDC2', CD1c+CD4+HLA-DR+, 2.41%), Langerhans cells ('Lang', CD1a+Langerin+, 2.13%), and plasmacytoid dendritic cells ('pDC', CD123+, 0.33%).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from phenotypic identification shown in Figure 4A.

claim: An immunosuppressive TIM3+ subpopulation was identifiable in both classical dendritic cell subgroups.
source: In both the two classical dendritic cell subgroups an immunosuppressive TIM3+ subpopulation was identifiable, while in the pDC group a small subpopulation was found to express PD-L1.
evidence: This is a finding from phenotypic identification.

claim: A small subpopulation of pDC was found to express PD-L1.
source: In both the two classical dendritic cell subgroups an immunosuppressive TIM3+ subpopulation was identifiable, while in the pDC group a small subpopulation was found to express PD-L1.
evidence: This is a finding from phenotypic identification.

claim: No immunosuppressive subpopulation was identified among the Langerhans cells.
source: No immunosuppressive subpopulation was identified among the Langerhans cells.
evidence: This is a negative finding from phenotypic identification.

claim: In active cases, there was a stronger spatial association between active Th and active Tcy.
source: In active cases, it was possible to identify a stronger spatial association between active Th and active Tcy, while the same association was weaker in transition cases and disappeared in exhausted ones.
evidence: This is a finding from neighborhood analysis shown in Figure 5A.

claim: The association between active Th and active Tcy was weaker in transition cases and disappeared in exhausted cases.
source: In active cases, it was possible to identify a stronger spatial association between active Th and active Tcy, while the same association was weaker in transition cases and disappeared in exhausted ones.
evidence: This is a finding from neighborhood analysis shown in Figures 5A and 5B.

claim: In active cases, TIM3+ macrophages interacted with CD69+TIM3+ Th.
source: In active cases, TIM3+ macrophages interacted with CD69+TIM3+ Th, as well as cDC1 expressing TIM3 interacted with TIM3+ Treg, possibly limiting their suppressive effect on the Tcy.
evidence: This is a finding from neighborhood analysis shown in Figure 5A.

claim: In active cases, cDC1 expressing TIM3 interacted with TIM3+ Treg, possibly limiting their suppressive effect on Tcy.
source: In active cases, TIM3+ macrophages interacted with CD69+TIM3+ Th, as well as cDC1 expressing TIM3 interacted with TIM3+ Treg, possibly limiting their suppressive effect on the Tcy.
evidence: This is a finding from neighborhood analysis with speculative interpretation shown in Figure 5A.

claim: The detection of the interaction of Langerhans cells with the epithelium was considered as positive control and proof of concept for the neighborhood analysis method.
source: The detection of the interaction of Langerhans cells with the epithelium, identifiable in both functional groups, was considered as positive control and proof of concept for the method.
evidence: This is stated as a validation of the neighborhood analysis method.

claim: 4 out of 8 melanomas with a brisk TILs pattern proved active by qPCR.
source: 4/8 melanomas with a brisk TILs pattern, and 3/7 with non-brisk TILs pattern proved active, confirming that we could subclassify from a functional point of view also metastatic lesions (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a finding from qPCR validation shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: 3 out of 7 melanomas with non-brisk TILs pattern proved active by qPCR.
source: 4/8 melanomas with a brisk TILs pattern, and 3/7 with non-brisk TILs pattern proved active, confirming that we could subclassify from a functional point of view also metastatic lesions (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a finding from qPCR validation shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: The 'IFNg-high' sample had more proteins (324) compared to 'LAG3-high' (93) and 'none' (134) samples.
source: The results showed a higher number of proteins identified in the 'IFNg-high' sample (324) compared to 'LAG3-high' (93) and 'none' (134), with almost two thirds of them (210/324) not shared with the other two samples and enriched in proteins involved in different inflammatory pathways (innate immunity, TNFR1 signalling pathway, FAS signalling pathway, T cell receptor and Fc-epsilon receptor signalling pathway), including the interferon gamma-mediated signaling pathway.
evidence: This is a finding from shotgun proteomics shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: 210 out of 324 proteins in the 'IFNg-high' sample were not shared with the other two samples and were enriched in proteins involved in different inflammatory pathways.
source: The results showed a higher number of proteins identified in the 'IFNg-high' sample (324) compared to 'LAG3-high' (93) and 'none' (134), with almost two thirds of them (210/324) not shared with the other two samples and enriched in proteins involved in different inflammatory pathways (innate immunity, TNFR1 signalling pathway, FAS signalling pathway, T cell receptor and Fc-epsilon receptor signalling pathway), including the interferon gamma-mediated signaling pathway.
evidence: This is a finding from shotgun proteomics and pathway analysis shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: OX40 was strongly correlated with Ki-67 and PD-1, confirming its role in sustaining Tcy clonal expansion.
source: OX40 was strongly correlated with Ki-67 and PD-1, confirming its role in sustaining Tcy clonal expansion (Huang et al., 2015).
evidence: This is a finding from the functional analysis with citation to Huang et al., 2015.

claim: No correlation was found between LAG3 and TIM3.
source: We didn't instead find correlation between LAG3 and TIM3.
evidence: This is a negative finding from the functional analysis.

claim: LAG3 is expressed very early and only transiently during T cell activation.
source: This could be due to the fact that LAG3 is expressed very early and only transiently during T cell activation (Andrews et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated with citation to Andrews et al., 2017.

claim: Persistent T cell activation with sustained expression of LAG3 together with other exhaustion markers results in T cell dysfunction.
source: Persistent T cell activation with sustained expression of LAG3 together with other exhaustion markers (e.g. PD-L1) results in T cell dysfunction (Andrews et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated with citation to Andrews et al., 2017.

claim: LAG3+Tregs have been shown to suppress DC maturation.
source: LAG3+Tregs have been shown to suppress DC maturation (Spranger et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated with citation to Spranger et al., 2016.

claim: Only a minority (15%) of patients presented with all active cores.
source: Only a minority (15%) of patients presented with all active cores, and 30% of patients presented with at least one active core, whereas the great majority of the patients presented with only exhausted or transition areas at the moment in which the melanoma was removed.
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the patient-level analysis.

claim: 30% of patients presented with at least one active core.
source: Only a minority (15%) of patients presented with all active cores, and 30% of patients presented with at least one active core, whereas the great majority of the patients presented with only exhausted or transition areas at the moment in which the melanoma was removed.
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the patient-level analysis.

claim: The percentage of patients that obtains a durable response with single agent checkpoint inhibition therapy lies between 15% and 30%.
source: Since the percentage of patients that obtains a durable response with single agent checkpoint inhibition therapy (Ribas and Flaherty, 2015; Ribas et al., 2016; Robert et al., 2015) lies between 15% and 30%, and since Krieg et al. (2018) reported that anti-PD-1 immunotherapy supports functionally activated T cells, it is tempting to speculate that the 'mostly active' TILs cases could correspond to the responders to immunotherapy, while the 'mostly exhausted' cases could benefit instead from combination approaches with immunotherapy and other type of therapies in order to rescue the exhausted T cells.
evidence: This is stated with citations to Ribas and Flaherty, 2015; Ribas et al., 2016; Robert et al., 2015.

claim: The 'mostly active' TILs cases could correspond to the responders to immunotherapy.
source: Since the percentage of patients that obtains a durable response with single agent checkpoint inhibition therapy (Ribas and Flaherty, 2015; Ribas et al., 2016; Robert et al., 2015) lies between 15% and 30%, and since Krieg et al. (2018) reported that anti-PD-1 immunotherapy supports functionally activated T cells, it is tempting to speculate that the 'mostly active' TILs cases could correspond to the responders to immunotherapy, while the 'mostly exhausted' cases could benefit instead from combination approaches with immunotherapy and other type of therapies in order to rescue the exhausted T cells.
evidence: This is explicitly stated as speculation by the authors.

claim: The 'mostly exhausted' cases could benefit from combination approaches with immunotherapy and other therapies to rescue exhausted T cells.
source: Since the percentage of patients that obtains a durable response with single agent checkpoint inhibition therapy (Ribas and Flaherty, 2015; Ribas et al., 2016; Robert et al., 2015) lies between 15% and 30%, and since Krieg et al. (2018) reported that anti-PD-1 immunotherapy supports functionally activated T cells, it is tempting to speculate that the 'mostly active' TILs cases could correspond to the responders to immunotherapy, while the 'mostly exhausted' cases could benefit instead from combination approaches with immunotherapy and other type of therapies in order to rescue the exhausted T cells.
evidence: This is explicitly stated as speculation by the authors.

claim: Spontaneous melanoma regression is present in only 10-35% of melanomas.
source: Since spontaneous melanoma regression, present in only 10–35% of the melanomas, is considered to be the end-results of the melanoma-eliminating capacities of active TILs, we also studied the association of activation of TILs with early and late regression (Botella-Estrada et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated with citation to Botella-Estrada et al., 2014.

claim: Spontaneous melanoma regression is considered to be the end-result of the melanoma-eliminating capacities of active TILs.
source: Since spontaneous melanoma regression, present in only 10–35% of the melanomas, is considered to be the end-results of the melanoma-eliminating capacities of active TILs, we also studied the association of activation of TILs with early and late regression (Botella-Estrada et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citation to Botella-Estrada et al., 2014.

claim: In late regression, a network of activating interactions between active Tcy and active Th was present.
source: In late regression, a network of activating interactions between active Tcy and active Th was Present. Few immune suppressing interactions could be observed, in particular between Treg-CD69+TIM3+Th-Exhausted Tcy (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is a finding from neighborhood analysis shown in Figure 3C.

claim: In late regression, few immune suppressing interactions could be observed, particularly between Treg-CD69+TIM3+Th-Exhausted Tcy.
source: In late regression, a network of activating interactions between active Tcy and active Th was Present. Few immune suppressing interactions could be observed, in particular between Treg-CD69+TIM3+Th-Exhausted Tcy (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is a finding from neighborhood analysis shown in Figure 3C.

claim: In early regression, the interactions between active Th and active Tcy disappeared.
source: In early regression, the interactions between active Th and active Tcy disappeared in this group, to leave space to aggregates of B cells located in strict proximity with anergic, proliferating and active T cells and probably stimulated by TIM3+cDC2, counterbalancing the effect of the immune stimulation between cDC1 and active Th (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is a finding from neighborhood analysis shown in Figure 3D.

claim: In early regression, aggregates of B cells were located in strict proximity with anergic, proliferating and active T cells.
source: In early regression, the interactions between active Th and active Tcy disappeared in this group, to leave space to aggregates of B cells located in strict proximity with anergic, proliferating and active T cells and probably stimulated by TIM3+cDC2, counterbalancing the effect of the immune stimulation between cDC1 and active Th (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is a finding from neighborhood analysis shown in Figure 3D.

claim: The study included 29 invasive primary cutaneous melanomas from the University Hospitals Leuven.
source: Twenty-nine invasive primary cutaneous melanomas from the Department of Pathology of the University Hospitals Leuven (KU Leuven), Belgium, were classified based on the H and E staining according to the pattern of the inflammatory infiltrate into brisk (six cases) and non-brisk (23 cases).
evidence: This describes the sample cohort used in the study.

claim: Six cases were classified as brisk and 23 cases as non-brisk.
source: Twenty-nine invasive primary cutaneous melanomas from the Department of Pathology of the University Hospitals Leuven (KU Leuven), Belgium, were classified based on the H and E staining according to the pattern of the inflammatory infiltrate into brisk (six cases) and non-brisk (23 cases).
evidence: This describes the distribution of morphological classifications in the cohort.

claim: The cohort included 24 superficial spreading melanomas, three nodular melanomas, and two lentigo maligna melanomas.
source: According to their subtype, 24 superficial spreading melanomas, three nodular melanomas, and two lentigo maligna melanoma were included.
evidence: This describes the histological subtypes in the cohort.

claim: All patients in the cohort were diagnosed between 2005 and 2010, before the era of immunotherapy.
source: All the patients in our cohort were diagnosed between 2005 and 2010, before the era of immunotherapy (both in metastatic and adjuvant setting).
evidence: This describes the temporal characteristics of the cohort.

claim: All patients received only surgery (broad excision) as first-line therapy.
source: Because only primary melanomas were included, all the patients received only surgery (broad excision) as first-line therapy.
evidence: This describes the treatment received by patients in the cohort.

claim: No significant differences were found between the 'Active' and 'Exhausted' groups according to age (t-test p.value = 0.6776382).
source: We did not find any significant differences between the 'Active' and 'Exhausted' groups according to age (t-test p.value = 0.6776382), gender (chisq-test p.value = 0.5814) or tumor location (chisq-test p.value = 0.1531).
evidence: This is a statistical finding from the analysis of patient characteristics.

claim: No significant differences were found between the 'Active' and 'Exhausted' groups according to gender (chisq-test p.value = 0.5814).
source: We did not find any significant differences between the 'Active' and 'Exhausted' groups according to age (t-test p.value = 0.6776382), gender (chisq-test p.value = 0.5814) or tumor location (chisq-test p.value = 0.1531).
evidence: This is a statistical finding from the analysis of patient characteristics.

claim: No significant differences were found between the 'Active' and 'Exhausted' groups according to tumor location (chisq-test p.value = 0.1531).

evidence: This is a statistical finding from the analysis of patient characteristics.

claim: A total of 60 cores were available for analysis after TMA processing.
source: After processing, cutting and staining of the TMA blocks, a total of 60 cores were available for analysis.
evidence: This describes the final sample size for analysis.

claim: 179,304 out of 242,224 cells (74.02%) were included for further analysis based on inclusion criteria.
source: Based on the inclusion criteria described in the methods, 179,304 out of 242,224 cells (74.02%) were included for further analysis.
evidence: This describes the cell-level sample size after quality control.

claim: The functional clustering resulted in a total number of 47 functional cell populations.
source: The functional clustering resulted in a total number of 47 functional cell populations (Figure 4A).
evidence: This describes the result of functional clustering shown in Figure 4A.

claim: The MILAN protocol allows safe detection of most antigens surviving routine processing, even after 30 cycles.
source: In conclusion, we believe that the MILAN protocol allows to safely detect most antigens surviving routine processing, even after 30 cycles, with variation in intensity within the variance of the technique itself.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion about the technical capabilities of the method.

claim: The variation for repeated staining on different sections averages 3.1% (range 0-12.3%).
source: In our previous publication, it is shown that the variation for repeated staining on different sections averages 3.1% (range 0–12.3%).
evidence: This describes the technical reproducibility of the MILAN method with reference to previous publication.

claim: Repeated staining while multiplexing (10 rounds) is usually less than 15% with some exceptions.
source: Repeated staining while multiplexing (10 rounds) is usually less than 15% with some exceptions (e.g keratin 19).
evidence: This describes the technical reproducibility of the MILAN method.

claim: Only about 2-3% of all antibodies used are made unreactive just after a single stripping session.
source: In addition, we have found that only about 2–3% of all antibodies used are made unreactive just after a single stripping session.
evidence: This describes the technical characteristics of the MILAN method.
